answer: Give every agent a juniper-like anchor: one identity, one hardware-attested sequential work chain. On joining, the agent's enclave starts a chained verifiable-delay sequence whose outputs must arrive on a fixed cadence, like tides of an ocean that cannot be hurried. Each proof is bound to that enclave, so one device advances exactly one chain at full speed. An attacker running a relic farm of fakes must split the same hardware across many chains; every chain then lags, misses rewards, and is flagged. Cloning costs full-rate hardware per identity, so Sybil scale buys no advantage.
